input.quote: 15.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Governing law is New York law (Section 15.5, and the same for the side Letter at p0671), which matches our preferred position. The dispute forum is arbitration rather than New York County courts, but it is not foreign arbitration: it is administered by JAMS under its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures with proceedings in English, patent/trademark scope and validity disputes are carved out to the courts of the granting country (15.6(h)), Program Invention ownership goes to U.S. patent counsel under U.S. patent law (15.6(i)), and either Party may seek interim or equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction (15.6(j)). That is well outside walk-away territory (vendor home-jurisdiction law or arbitration seated abroad) and satisfies the rule on its material terms. Two sub-points noted rather than flagged: the arbitral seat and number of arbitrators in 15.6(a) are redacted ([***]), so we should confirm on turn that the seat is in the United States (ideally New York, New York), and 15.6(f) bars punitive/exemplary damages in arbitration — a mutual limitation that does not disadvantage us asymmetrically.
